facts.text: Sachin Tendulkar played 200 Tests but only 199 for India — 1 match was for ICC World XI vs Australia (2005 Super Series). The kaggle_batting table only has his 199 India innings; the ICC World XI innings is missing from the data. When queried, show 199 matches from data but mention the 200th
Pakistan played home Tests and ODIs in UAE (2009-2023) due to the 2009 Lahore attack on the Sri Lanka team. Treat UAE venues (Dubai, Abu Dhabi, Sharjah) as Pakistan 'home' for this period
Afghanistan's home matches have been hosted in India (Dehradun, Greater Noida, Lucknow, Chandigarh) since they have no ICC-approved home ground
Zimbabwe was suspended from Test cricket 2006-2011. Their Test numbering has a gap in this period
Bangladesh played their first Test in 2000 vs India, but early 'home' Tests were sometimes at neutral venues
South Africa was banned from international cricket 1970-1991 due to apartheid. No Tests/ODIs exist for this period
Ireland and Afghanistan became Test nations in 2017. Their Test data starts from 2018
The ICC World Test Championship started in 2019-2021. WTC finals are held at neutral venues (Lord's 2021, The Oval 2023)
In T20 cricket, a Super Over is used to break ties. The match winner is the Super Over winner — the main match is NOT recorded as a tie
Before 2000, there were only 2 tied Tests in history (Brisbane 1960, Madras 1986). A tie is when both teams are all out with equal scores. A draw is when time runs out
The IPL (Indian Premier League) started in 2008. In Cricsheet data, use event_name = 'Indian Premier League'
The BBL (Big Bash League) started in 2011-12. In Cricsheet data, use event_name = 'Big Bash League'
In Cricsheet data, IT20 = men's T20 International, T20 = generic T20, ODM = men's ODI domestic. For international T20s, use match_type IN ('T20', 'IT20')
Cricsheet player names use initials (SR Tendulkar, V Kohli, SPD Smith). Kaggle uses full names (Sachin Tendulkar, Virat Kohli, Steven Smith). Always use player_map to cross-reference
Don Bradman's Test average of 99.94 is the single most famous statistic in cricket. He needed just 4 runs in his final innings to average 100 but was bowled for a duck
Brian Lara holds the record for the highest individual Test score: 400* vs England at Antigua, 2004
Jim Laker took 19 wickets in a single Test (19/90) vs Australia at Old Trafford, 1956 — the best match bowling figures ever
A batsman's 'not out' innings should NOT count as a dismissal when calculating batting average. Average = total runs / times dismissed
In Test cricket, innings 3 and 4 are the 'second innings' of each team. 4th innings is typically the final run chase and has historically lower averages due to deteriorating pitch

Some players have represented multiple countries: Kepler Wessels (Australia then South Africa), Ed Joyce (England then Ireland), Eoin Morgan (Ireland then England), Luke Ronchi (Australia then New Zealand)
West Indies is a multi-nation team representing Caribbean countries (Jamaica, Barbados, Trinidad, Guyana, etc.). Their home venues span multiple countries
The Ashes is a Test series between Australia and England, held roughly every 2 years alternating between the two countries. In Cricsheet, look for series/event names containing 'Ashes'
ODI cricket started in 1971. The first Cricket World Cup was in 1975. T20 Internationals started in 2005. The first T20 World Cup was in 2007
In older Test matches (pre-2000), ball-by-ball data is not available in Cricsheet. Only scorecard data from Kaggle tables covers the full 1877-present range
Day-night Tests (with pink ball) started in 2015. They can affect batting stats due to different conditions under lights
The DLS method (Duckworth-Lewis-Stern) is used to adjust targets in rain-affected limited-overs matches. outcome_method = 'D/L' or 'DLS' in the data
Mankading (now called 'running out the non-striker') was made legal without warning from 2022 onwards. It appears as kind = 'run out' in wickets data
In Cricsheet data, over_num is 0-indexed. So over_num = 0 is the first over, over_num = 19 is the 20th (last) over in T20. Powerplay = over_num 0-5, death = 15-19
Several countries have changed names in cricket records: Rhodesia became Zimbabwe, Ceylon became Sri Lanka, East Africa and ICC Associates teams have played in World Cups
When a Test match is 'abandoned' or 'no result', it doesn't count in win/loss records but may still appear in the matches table
